text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: `DB_CONN_MAXED` for postgres-primary in us-west-2. severity: P0. pg_bouncer connections >= 95% for > 30s.
PagerDuty: Trigger: DB_CONN_MAXED -> Assigned: Mike (on-call)
Mike: acked. I’m looking. Paging into #eng-oncall.
Mike: seeing connection_errors and a spike in `pg_stat_activity` where lots of app workers are in state = 'idle in transaction' and waiting on auth.
Sarah: did we rotate DB credentials this morning? I deployed a token rotation at 03:10 UTC for the read-replica rollout.
Jen: yes, there was a secret rotation automated job at 03:08. Some services were updated but not all.
Mike: that would explain auth failures leading to reconnect storms. apps try to reconnect, hit max_connections, pgbouncer queues.
Dave: paging in for handoff in 15. If this is auth rotation, we need to pause the rotation or re-enable old creds.
Mike: current metrics: `pgbouncer-clients` = 4900/5000, `pg_backend_count` = 480, auth_failures per sec ~ 120. Latency for short queries 200ms -> 2s. Customer impact: API timeouts and increased 5xxs on chat generation routes.
Sarah: rolling back rotation now — canceling job and re-propagating previous secret. Command I ran: `kubectl -n infra delete job/db-cred-rotator-2026-03-15`
Mike: thanks. Also temporarily bumped pgbouncer pool to accept more clients (patched config) and reloaded: `kubectl -n infra exec pgbouncer-0 -- pgbouncer -R` (reload). That buys us time.
Jen: ps aux from one app host shows 800 concurrent worker processes each opening 2 db connections (total ~1600) — connection storm makes sense. Can we enable aggressive client-side backoff?
Dave: for immediate mitigation: (1) increase pgbouncer max_clients by 20% (done), (2) set `max_connections` on PG to allow +100 (ops approved), (3) enable app-level jitter/backoff via feature flag to stagger reconnects.
Mike: applying DB change now: `ALTER SYSTEM SET max_connections = 1200; SELECT pg_reload_conf();`
incident-bot: Note: change performed by Mike at 1789123802.
Mike: DB accepted new connections. Watching queues. pgbouncer queue length dropping from 800 -> 120 over 4m.
Sarah: re-propagation of old secret to a subset finished; apps that were still failing are now getting successful auth. Errors falling.
Jen: running a cleanup script to terminate very old idle transactions: `SELECT pid, age(now(), query_start), state FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE state='idle in transaction' AND age(now(), query_start) > interval '5 minutes';` then `SELECT pg_terminate_backend(pid);` (run carefully).
Mike: ran terminate for 120 stale backends. queue length down to ~30. Latency returning to baseline.
Dave: customer update drafted: "We experienced connection saturation due to an unexpected credential rotation impact. We've rolled back the rotation, applied mitigations (connection pool increase, terminating stale sessions), and are monitoring. Temporary increased capacity applied to protect in-flight requests." Want me to post?
Mike: yes go ahead. Include ETA for full recovery: 30m.
Jen: also flagging engineering change: rotation job should do canary propagation across services with health-check gating — we need rollout orchestration in the secrets operator.
Sarah: logging note: rotation job missed the `--grace-period` flag which should have signaled apps to warm reload. Filed issue: infra#4521.
PagerDuty: Escalation: if not acked by next responder within 10m, escalate to SRE lead. (auto)
Mike: I'm handing off to Dave since I need to support a live customer call. Dave, take the thread.
Dave: taking over. timeline so far: rotate -> auth errors -> reconnect storm -> pgbouncer queueing -> increased pgbouncer + pg connections -> terminate stale sessions -> stable. Monitoring CPU on primary at 85% (was 95%).
Dave: next steps: (1) run a targeted smoke test across regions to validate no lingering auth failures, (2) revert temporary db config after traffic stabilizes, (3) implement rollout gating in rotation job.
Jen: smoke tests start in 2m. Running: `curl -v https://api.internal/healthcheck -H "X-Test: db-conn-check"` against 10 hosts.
Dave: smoke tests show 2/10 hosts still had transient 401s earlier but now all 10 pass.
Mike: thanks. Are we ready to set this to 'monitoring' in PagerDuty?
Dave: yes. PagerDuty status -> Monitoring.
incident-bot: PagerDuty incident 1789123456 transitioned to MONITORING by Dave at 1789124205.
Sarah: follow-up: propose adding a small random jitter (0-3s) to reconnect loops in the common db client lib to avoid synchronized reconnect storms. Filed PR draft: https://git.internal/redwood/infralib/pull/231
Jen: also add health-check gating to secrets rotator: require <1% auth failures during canary to proceed.
Dave: noted. Ops checklist updated and handoff to post-incident review owner Sarah. I'll create a short postmortem draft after monitoring completes.
Mike: thx all — great triage. :tada:
Dave: closing loop in 1h if metrics stable. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: This thread will be archived once incident is closed.
